study_identification_part.si4_title: Cell type-specific manifestations of cortical thickness heterogeneity in schizophrenia

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: To determine whether cortical thickness (CTh) heterogeneity in schizophrenia relates to interregional variation in distinct neural cell types, as inferred from established gene expression data and person-specific genomic variation.

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa7_association_analysis: Spatial correlations between regional CTh deviations and cell-type gene expression maps; Ansari-Bradley test for dispersion of correlations; Ward's linkage clustering for subtyping; Partial correlations between polygenic scores and mean CTh deviations, accounting for sex, genome-wide sczPRS, and familial relatedness.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: Cortical thickness heterogeneity in schizophrenia relates to inter-individual variation in cell-type specific functions, allowing for the stratification of patients into biologically validated subtypes based on genomic, transcriptomic, and brain phenotypic data.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa9_key_findings_detailed: Patient CTh deviations from a normative model were explained by interregional gene expression of five neural cell types, allowing stratification into subtypes. A neuronal/endothelial subtype (22% of patients) showed a correlation between CTh deviations and neuronal/endothelial-specific polygenic risk for schizophrenia (r=-0.40). A glia/OPC subtype (43% of patients) showed a correlation between CTh deviations and glia/OPC-specific polygenic risk (r=-0.30), validating the biological basis of the subtypes.

caa10_key_limitations.answer: 1. The inference of cell-type gene expression relies on data from healthy postmortem brains, not the individuals being studied. 2. The predictive power of polygenic risk may be weakened for subtypes with mixed cellular patterns. 3. The estimation of cell type transcriptional maps depends on the source data used for gene sets, which can lead to different results compared to other studies (e.g., using mouse vs. human data).
caa10_key_limitations.supporting_text: First, regional nonuniformity in cell type-speci /uniFB01 c gene expression may depend on cell numbers and/or single-cell transcription levels... Second, patterns of CTh alterations that do not map neatly onto speci /uniFB01 c cell types may weaken the predictive power of polygenic risk... Third, cell type associations with MRIderived phenotypes hinge on the estimation of cell type transcriptional maps.

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa11_application_notes: The study presents a novel multi-scale framework that integrates in vivo MRI (via normative modeling), ex vivo transcriptomics (gene expression maps), and patient-specific genomics (polygenic scores) to deconstruct phenotypic heterogeneity, link it to underlying cellular mechanisms, and validate the findings.

general_note_part.gn1_general_notes: A key innovation of this study is the validation of imaging-based patient subtypes using person-specific genetic data (cell-type-specific polygenic scores), providing a strong link between macroscopic brain alterations and individual genetic liability. The work successfully stratified patients into distinct neurobiological subgroups (e.g., neuronal-related vs. glia-related pathology), demonstrating a path towards precision medicine in psychiatry.
